---
title: "How much of the program should go to exotic germplasm?"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, dpi = 110)
```

Elite programs narrow over time. Each cycle crosses the best lines with each
other, and alleles that are not in those lines are lost for good. Exotic
germplasm, such as wild soybean (*Glycine soja*) or old landraces, still
carries some of that lost variation. It is also far worse for yield, so every
cross to it costs gain now in the hope of gain later.

Most programs handle this with **bridging crosses**: cross an elite line to
an exotic, backcross once to elite, select among the progeny, and let only the
best enter the elite crossing block. That raises two design questions:

* What share of the crosses should be bridging crosses?
* Should bridge-derived lines compete with elite lines for parent slots on
  merit, or get a few **reserved** slots so their diversity survives early
  selection?

This is a long-term question, so it needs many cycles and a fair number of
replicates. It also needs a custom program, which is what
`alphasim_program()` is for.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidyagsim)
library(AlphaSimR)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## The program

Each replicate starts by making an elite pool. Half of the founders go
through eight generations of selection, which raises their mean but uses up
much of their genetic variance. The other half stay unselected and play the
exotic accessions. Gains are measured from the elite pool's starting point,
in its own genetic standard deviations.

Every cycle then makes 40 crosses. A share `bridge_share` of them are
bridging crosses (elite × exotic, then one backcross to an elite parent), and
the rest are elite × elite. All lines are advanced three generations and
phenotyped in two reps. Then 15 parents are chosen for the next cycle,
either all on merit (`reserved = 0`) or with `reserved` slots kept for the
best bridge-derived lines. The number of crosses is the same for every
design, so every design has the same budget.

```{r}
program <- function(founders, SP, bridge_share, reserved, n_crosses = 40, per_cross = 10,
                    n_parents = 15, burn_in = 8, cycles = 15) {
  # An elite pool narrowed by earlier selection, and unselected exotic accessions.
  elite <- founders[1:30]
  exotic <- founders[31:60]
  for (g in seq_len(burn_in)) {
    elite <- selectInd(setPheno(elite), 10)
    elite <- self(randCross(elite, nCrosses = 30, nProgeny = 2))
  }
  elite <- self(self(elite))
  tracker <- asr_tracker(elite)
  parents <- selectInd(setPheno(elite, reps = 4), n_parents)

  for (cycle in seq_len(cycles)) {
    n_bridge <- round(bridge_share * n_crosses)
    lines <- self(randCross(parents, nCrosses = n_crosses - n_bridge), nProgeny = per_cross)
    lines <- setPheno(self(self(lines)), reps = 2)
    if (n_bridge > 0) {
      # Elite x exotic, then one backcross to an elite parent.
      f1 <- hybridCross(parents, exotic, crossPlan = cbind(sample(nInd(parents), n_bridge, TRUE),
                                                           sample(nInd(exotic), n_bridge, TRUE)))
      bc1 <- hybridCross(f1, parents, crossPlan = cbind(seq_len(n_bridge),
                                                        sample(nInd(parents), n_bridge, TRUE)))
      bridge <- setPheno(self(self(self(bc1, nProgeny = per_cross))), reps = 2)
      parents <- if (reserved > 0) {
        c(selectInd(lines, n_parents - reserved), selectInd(bridge, reserved))
      } else {
        selectInd(c(lines, bridge), n_parents)
      }
    } else {
      parents <- selectInd(lines, n_parents)
    }
    tracker$record(parents, year = cycle * 4, released_lines = selectInd(parents, 3))
  }
  asr_summary(tracker)
}
```

The designs are no bridging, then 10%, 25% or 50% bridging crosses, with or
without three reserved parent slots:

```{r}
spec <- alphasim_program(program, bridge_share = tune(), reserved = tune(),
                         founders = asr_founders(n_founders = 60, n_chr = 10, seg_sites = 150, qtl_per_chr = 15))
designs <- rbind(data.frame(bridge_share = 0, reserved = 0),
                 expand.grid(bridge_share = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5), reserved = c(0, 3)))
res <- tune_grid(spec, sim_replicates(20, seed = 1), grid = designs,
                 metrics = sim_metric_set(release_gain, genetic_variance),
                 control = control_sim(save_outcomes = TRUE))
```

## Short term against long term

```{r, fig.alt = "Mean genetic value of the parents over 60 years for each design. Bridging designs start lower and overtake the elite-only program after about 30 to 40 years."}
traj <- collect_trajectories(res)
avg <- aggregate(mean ~ bridge_share + reserved + year, data = traj, FUN = mean)
avg$design <- ifelse(avg$bridge_share == 0, "Elite only",
                     paste0(100 * avg$bridge_share, "% bridging"))
avg$slots <- ifelse(avg$reserved == 0, "Parents chosen on merit", "3 parent slots reserved for bridge lines")
elite_only <- avg[avg$bridge_share == 0, ]
plot_data <- rbind(avg[avg$bridge_share > 0, ],
                   transform(elite_only, slots = "Parents chosen on merit"),
                   transform(elite_only, slots = "3 parent slots reserved for bridge lines"))

ggplot(plot_data, aes(year, mean, colour = design)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~slots) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Elite only" = "black", "10% bridging" = "#9ECAE9",
                                 "25% bridging" = "#4C78A8", "50% bridging" = "#1F3B63")) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean genetic value of parents\n(elite genetic SDs)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Exotic crosses cost gain early and pay it back later") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Zoom in on the first and last cycles to see the trade:

```{r}
first_last <- avg[avg$year %in% c(4, 60), ]
first_last <- reshape(first_last[, c("design", "slots", "year", "mean")], idvar = c("design", "slots"),
                      timevar = "year", direction = "wide")
names(first_last)[3:4] <- c("after_1_cycle", "after_15_cycles")
first_last[order(first_last$slots, first_last$design), ]
```

* **Bridging costs gain at first.** After one cycle, the programs with 50%
  bridging are about a sixth of a standard deviation behind. The 10% programs
  lose little or nothing.
* **The elite-only program runs out of steam.** Its gain per cycle slows as
  its genetic variance is used up. Bridging programs that choose parents on
  merit pass it after about 25 to 30 years (seven cycles), and those with
  reserved slots after about 40.
* **After 15 cycles every bridging design is ahead.** Because the designs
  share seeds, the comparison is paired. Here is the difference between the
  elite-only program and 50% bridging on merit:

```{r}
m <- collect_metrics(res, type = "wide")
m$design <- ifelse(m$bridge_share == 0, "Elite only", paste0(100 * m$bridge_share, "% bridging"))
cfg <- function(share, slots) m$.config[m$bridge_share == share & m$reserved == slots]
compare_designs(res, cfg(0, 0), cfg(0.5, 0), metric = "release_gain")
```

## What the reserved slots buy

Chosen on merit, 25% or 50% bridging ends up ahead of 10%. With reserved
slots the share of bridging crosses matters less, and the slots make a
different difference: the diversity that is left.

```{r, fig.alt = "Genetic value of released lines against remaining genetic variance after 15 cycles. Reserved slots keep far more genetic variance at similar gain."}
ggplot(m, aes(genetic_variance, release_gain, colour = factor(reserved), label = design)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = release_gain - release_gain_se, ymax = release_gain + release_gain_se), width = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.9, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("0" = "#F58518", "3" = "#4C78A8"), labels = c("On merit", "3 reserved")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.2)) +
  labs(x = "Genetic variance left after 15 cycles (relative to the elite pool at the start)",
       y = "Released lines (elite genetic SDs)", colour = "Parent slots")
```

When bridge lines compete on merit, few of them make it into the crossing
block. With 10% or 25% bridging the program ends up nearly as narrow as the
elite-only one, and even 50% keeps less than half the starting variance. With
three slots kept for them, the program finishes with about as much genetic
variance as it started with (0.8 to 1.1 times), at gains close to the best on merit.
That is room for the next
decades of selection, and the simulation says it costs little here.

## Caveats, and making it yours

This model is generous to the exotics. They come from the same founder
population as the elite pool and differ only by not having been selected.
Real wild soybean carries many alleles that are bad in a cultivated
background, such as vining, pod shattering and small seed, so bridging costs
more and pays back more slowly. Ways to make the study closer to your
program:

* **Make the exotics worse.** Use a `setup` function in `asr_founders()` to
  build two populations, or select the exotic half *against* yield for a few
  generations during the burn-in.
* **Add a pre-breeding stage.** Run bridge lines through two or three cycles
  of their own selection before they can enter the elite block, and tune its
  length.
* **Use your own germplasm.** Load marker data for your elite lines and
  accessions with `asr_founders(haplotypes = )`.
* **Tune more of the balance.** Make `reserved`, the backcross generations
  and the share of the budget all `tune()` arguments, and search them with
  `tune_bayes()` with a constraint on `genetic_variance`.
